title: A Sensible Default
prompt:
Write `function greet(name, greeting = "Hello")` that returns `${greeting}, ${name}!`. `greet("Ada")` returns `Hello, Ada!`; `greet("Ada", "Bonjour")` returns `Bonjour, Ada!`.

Rules:
- The second parameter has a default value — no if-check.

tests.name: default kicks in
tests.code:
const fn = new Function(code + "\nreturn greet;");
if (fn()("Ada") !== "Hello, Ada!") throw new Error("greet('Ada') should be 'Hello, Ada!'.");
tests.hint: function greet(name, greeting = "Hello") — the default fills in when the argument is missing.

tests.name: override works
tests.code:
const fn = new Function(code + "\nreturn greet;");
if (fn()("Ada", "Bonjour") !== "Bonjour, Ada!") throw new Error("greet('Ada', 'Bonjour') should be 'Bonjour, Ada!'.");
tests.hint: A passed argument replaces the default.

tests.name: default in the signature, not an if
tests.hint: The = goes right in the signature. No branching required.
